title: 3rd Truth Ease Amid Speed And Multiplicity And The Gradelessness Of Power

questions.question: What main quality of creation is highlighted at the beginning of the passage about plants and animals?
questions.answer: Their creation is presented as happening very quickly while still being perfectly ordered and skillful.

questions.question: Which two groups of living things are especially pointed out in this truth?
questions.answer: Plants and animals.

questions.question: What seeming tension does the passage emphasize in the way beings are created?
questions.answer: They are made with speed and ease, yet also with careful artistry, value, and precision.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the relationship between abundance and distinction?
questions.answer: Even though creatures are many and mixed together, each still appears with its own worth and clear form.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of being alone can create in this way?
questions.answer: Only a uniquely powerful Creator for whom nothing is hard.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Creator’s power in relation to stars and atoms?
questions.answer: Creating the largest and the smallest is equally easy for Him.

questions.question: How is a whole species compared with one member of that species?
questions.answer: Bringing a whole species into being is no harder than bringing one individual into being.

questions.question: What comparison is made between reviving the earth and bringing a tree to life?
questions.answer: Both are described as equally easy for the Creator.

questions.question: What does the example of a huge tree and a tiny seed show?
questions.answer: Size does not make any difference to Divine power.

questions.question: Why does the passage say these acts are important for human reflection?
questions.answer: Because they happen openly before us and point us to the Creator’s limitless power.

questions.question: What central claim does the passage make about how living things are brought into existence?
questions.answer: They are created with total speed, ease, order, and excellence at the same time.

questions.question: Why is this combination of speed and precision significant?
questions.answer: Because such perfect results under those conditions cannot come from limited power.

questions.question: Besides speed and order, what other qualities are mentioned in creation?
questions.answer: Skill, ability, care, value, and distinctness.

questions.question: What problem does the passage say does not happen even though beings are numerous and mixed together?
questions.answer: There is no confusion and no shortcoming.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the absence of confusion in abundant creation?
questions.answer: It shows the work of one unmatched Creator with unrestricted power.

questions.question: How does the passage compare creating something universal and something particular?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for the Creator.

questions.question: What is meant by comparing the greatest thing with the smallest thing?
questions.answer: Divine power is not strained by scale, whether the object is immense or tiny.

questions.question: How does the passage use the earth and a tree to strengthen its argument?
questions.answer: It says giving life to the whole earth is just as easy as giving life to a tree.

questions.question: What role does direct observation play in the passage’s reasoning?
questions.answer: It argues that these realities are visible in the world around us, not just abstract ideas.

questions.question: What is the main message a thoughtful reader should take from this truth?
questions.answer: The order, abundance, and ease of creation point clearly to the oneness and limitless power of Allah.

questions.question: What does the verse at the start of this section point people toward using?
questions.answer: It points them toward using their reason and understanding.

questions.question: How does the passage connect reason with observing creation?
questions.answer: It treats creation as a sign that thoughtful people can read and understand.

questions.question: What features of creation are presented together instead of separately?
questions.answer: Fast production, easy production, careful design, and high value are presented together.

questions.question: Why is it important that beings are created in abundance?
questions.answer: Because abundance usually suggests sameness or disorder, yet here each being still has clear design and worth.

questions.question: What does the passage imply by saying nothing is difficult for that power?
questions.answer: Divine power has no limitation, weakness, or burden.

questions.question: How does the comparison between stars and atoms support belief in Divine power?
questions.answer: It shows that vast difference in size does not matter to the Creator at all.

questions.question: What does the comparison between a species and one individual teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that totality and single instances are equally within Divine control.

questions.question: What lesson comes from comparing the whole earth’s renewal with the life of one tree?
questions.answer: The same power that handles what looks enormous also handles what looks small with equal ease.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention a seed as small as a fingernail?
questions.answer: To show that producing tiny beginnings and massive outcomes both belong to the same effortless power.

questions.question: In one sentence, what is the overall argument of this passage?
questions.answer: The way creation appears—rapid, abundant, exact, and beautiful—shows the action of one all-powerful Creator.

questions.question: What kind of order does the passage describe in the creation of living beings?
questions.answer: It describes flawless order that appears even when creation is fast and widespread.

questions.question: How does the passage portray ease in creation?
questions.answer: It says beings are brought into existence without strain while still showing great mastery.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the artistic side of creation?
questions.answer: It presents created beings as finely made, purposeful, and skillfully distinguished.

questions.question: Why is intermingling mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: To show that even when many beings exist together, each remains properly formed and recognizable.

questions.question: What kind of cause would be needed to produce such results, according to the passage?
questions.answer: A single incomparable source of power with no difficulty in doing anything.

questions.question: How does the passage use contrast in size to make its point?
questions.answer: It contrasts huge and tiny things to show that both are equally easy for Divine power.

questions.question: What is the significance of saying a mountain-like tree and a tiny seed are equally easy to produce?
questions.answer: It means outcomes that seem vastly different to us are not different in difficulty for Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the Creator’s relationship to all levels of existence?
questions.answer: He governs and creates everything, from the smallest detail to the largest whole, with the same power.

questions.question: Why does the line about these deeds happening before our eyes matter?
questions.answer: It reminds us that the proof is visible in everyday reality.

questions.question: How would you summarize the evidence offered in this section?
questions.answer: The evidence is the visible world itself, where countless beings are created swiftly, abundantly, and perfectly.

questions.question: What is the subject of “The Third Truth”?
questions.answer: It is the meaning shown by the way living things are created with speed, order, ease, and value.

questions.question: Which aspect of creation would normally make careful distinction seem difficult?
questions.answer: Great abundance and mixing together would normally make distinction difficult.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens instead of confusion?
questions.answer: Every being is brought forth properly, skillfully, and without defect.

questions.question: How does the passage connect ability and order?
questions.answer: It presents true supreme ability as producing perfect order rather than disorder.

questions.question: What must be true of a power that creates this way?
questions.answer: It must be a power for which no task is difficult.

questions.question: What does the passage teach through the example of stars and atoms?
questions.answer: The Creator’s power is not measured by size or scale.

questions.question: How does the passage use the example of species and individuals?
questions.answer: It shows that creating many is no harder than creating one.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the earth coming to life and a tree coming to life?
questions.answer: Both acts are treated as equally easy for the same Divine power.

questions.question: What does the seed example add to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that even the tiniest beginning is produced by the same unrestricted power that creates immense forms.

questions.question: What conclusion should a student draw from all these comparisons?
questions.answer: Visible creation points to Allah’s unique and unlimited power and to His oneness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes the creation of plants and animals especially striking?
questions.answer: They are created quickly, easily, abundantly, and still with exact order and beauty.

questions.question: What four paired ideas work together in this description of creation?
questions.answer: Speed with order, ease with skill, abundance with value, and intermingling with distinction.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress that there is no confusion or deficiency?
questions.answer: Because that shows this is not random or weak production but precise creation.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from such precise and abundant creation?
questions.answer: It can only come from a uniquely powerful Creator.

questions.question: How does the passage define the reach of that power?
questions.answer: It describes it as a power to which every kind of creation is equally easy.

questions.question: In what way are stars and atoms used as teaching examples?
questions.answer: They illustrate that the largest and smallest things are the same before Divine power.

questions.question: Why are a species and a single member compared?
questions.answer: To show that multiplicity does not increase difficulty for Allah.

questions.question: What do the examples of the earth, a tree, and a seed have in common?
questions.answer: All of them show that what seems big or small to us makes no difference to the Creator’s ability.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying these deeds happen in front of our eyes?
questions.answer: The signs of Divine power are directly observable in the world we live in.

questions.question: What is the strongest overall inference from this passage?
questions.answer: The harmony of speed, abundance, precision, and ease in creation is a clear sign of Allah’s absolute power and unity.
